 Real won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Jose Mourinho.

 Sunday night could not get any better for Real Madrid fans.

 end of list When the action kicked off under the lights at Camp Nou for the Clasico, Jose Mourinho’s side were far from the favourites . But after 90 minutes of drama and fiery football, Real had the last laugh, beating rivals Barcelona 2-1 in a tantalising match.
 The victory has renewed belief among the Bernabeu faithful, who are counting on Mourinho to lead them back to glory days.
 Here are the key takeaways from Real’s El Clasico win against Barcelona:
 Real earn bragging rights and snap Barca’s perfect record
 Mbappe’s brace – which took his tally to 14 goals this season – was enough to silence the tens of thousands of Barcelona supporters at Camp Nou.
 With that, Los Blancos became the first side to beat Barcelona in the league this season, ending the Catalan club’s nine-game winning streak in the top flight. Had Barcelona won, they would have broken Real’s 1968-69 record for a best-ever start in the Spanish top flight.
 It also marked a second straight defeat for Hansi Flick’s side, coming only days after they fell to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.
 As for Real, victory brought home bragging rights. Real now lead the head-to-head record with 107 wins to Barca’s 106 in their all-time Clasico record.
 Dean Huijsen gives a thumbs-up after Real Madrid’s s El Clasico win over Barcelona [Alex Caparros/Getty Images] Mbappe hits a century of Real goals
 A day before the world tunes in to watch the Ballon d’Or ceremony for the best player of the 2025-26 season, Mbappe achieved another milestone.
 Advertisement The French forward’s brace brought up his 100th goal for Real across all competitions since joining in 2024 from PSG.
 The 27-year-old, the second-best La Liga scorer this season, is building on a remarkable performance last campaign, which saw him finish as La Liga and the Champions League’s top scorer, the World Cup Golden Boot winner and the all-time leading World Cup scorer.
 Those statistics have made him one of the frontrunners for the Ballon d’Or ahead of Monday’s gala in London.
 Real Madrid players celebrate Mbappe’s second goal [Josep Lago/AFP] Real are slowly closing the gap on Barcelona
 Defeats to Real Betis and Atletico Madrid last month shook Real’s top-flight campaign, but recent results reflect stability.
 Real have now won five matches in a row – three in La Liga and two in the UCL – and seem to be coming into strong form.
 Even though Sunday’s victory was just a second in eight games against Barcelona, Real are slowly reducing the gap on Barca this season, with just over a quarter of the season played.
 After 10 matches, they are third in the league standings on 24 points, three points behind Barcelona, while Atletico are sandwiched in between, sitting second with 25 points.
 Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe are two of their star players [Ana Beltran/Reuters] Can Mourinho bring Real back to glory days?
 The improvement in form suggests Mourinho’s Real can challenge Barcelona’s recent La Liga dominance in his first season back in Spain.
 After two seasons without trophies, Real turned to old boss Mourinho to find a way to stop Barca’s dominance.
 Although Mourinho has not won a league title since guiding Chelsea to the Premier League crown in 2014-15, his record as one of football’s most decorated managers remains formidable.
 Thirteen years after his first spell at Real ended, Mourinho’s return to the Clasico offered a chance to make an immediate statement, and victory over Barcelona made it all the sweeter.
 The result should also help to boost morale and build unity within the Real squad. ‌‌‌‌More importantly, Mourinho now has evidence that his methods can help return Real to the summit of Spanish football.
 “If we win today but lose at El Sardinero, it counts for nothing, because Madrid isn’t ‌‌‌‌playing ‌‌‌‌to win at the Camp Nou,” Mourinho said. “They’re playing to win the championship.”
 Mourinho has made his intentions clear.
 After celebrating Sunday’s Clasico win with his trademark knee slide, the 63-year-old manager knows his job is far from over.
 Advertisement Having led Real to three trophies during his first spell, including a record-breaking La Liga ⁠⁠⁠⁠triumph, Mourinho knows best what Real are capable of achieving.
